page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.4xlarge is an instance within the High Clock Speed instance family, engineered for compute-intensive tasks requiring elevated single-thread and sustained frequency capabilities. Powered by KVM virtualization, this server provides 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6462C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. Memory provisioning is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance does not bundle any local storage or hardware accelerators, leaving local storage at zero and GPU count at zero. Consequently, operating systems and persistent data must rely entirely on remote network block storage. For network transport, the configuration provides a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps, facilitating rapid communication with external storage volumes, cache nodes, and application services.

Cost efficiency is influenced primarily by the high-frequency processor allocation. For workloads that are constrained by execution latency or per-core license models rather than sheer memory size, the combination of 3.3 GHz clock frequency and dedicated core provisioning reduces processing times. However, the requirement for attached cloud storage represents an architectural tradeoff that must be factored into storage throughput planning.

The ecs.hfg8i.4xlarge is suitable for computational workloads benefiting from high clock frequencies, including application servers, relational database engines, game server hosting, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.4xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6462C processor operating at 3.3 GHz, alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached volumes for data retention and operating systems. Networking is provisioned with a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth. With its focus on fast processing speeds and a balanced memory footprint, this instance delivers strong execution efficiency for frequency-dependent workloads without the overhead of massive memory arrays. It is engineered for latency-sensitive applications, mid-sized database management systems, continuous integration builds, and high-throughput application serving.
